items.title: Section: Waves on a Torrent, Reflections in a Mirror — Five Similes for Consciousnesses That Coexist Without Truly Corresponding

items.zh: 何以故？由不與彼同緣轉故。如眼識雖與眼根俱轉，然不相應。此亦如是。應知此中，依少分相似道理，故得為喻。又如諸心所，雖心所性無有差別，然相異故，於一身中一時俱轉，互不相違。如是阿賴耶識與諸轉識，於一身中一時俱轉，當知更互亦不相違。又如於一瀑流，有多波浪一時而轉，互不相違。又如於一清淨鏡面，有多影像一時而轉，互不相違。如是於一阿賴耶識，有多轉識一時俱轉，當知更互亦不相違。又如一眼識，於一時間，於一事境唯取一類無異色相；或於一時，頓取非一種種色相。如眼識於眾色，如是耳識於眾聲、鼻識於眾香、舌識於眾味亦爾。又如身識，或於一時，於一事境唯取一類無異觸相；或於一時，頓取非一種種觸相。如是分別意識，於一時間，或取一境相，或取非一種種境相。當知道理亦不相違。
items.en:
Second, posing the question. Why is this?
Third, explaining; first, revealing the meaning. Because they do not operate upon the same object.
Second, similes for the characteristic; first, similes for phenomena co-arising; first, the eye-consciousness and eye faculty; first, establishing the analogy. Just as the eye-consciousness co-arises with the eye faculty yet does not correspond with it, so too is this the case here.
Second, the mental factors. Just as the various mental factors, though the mental nature is undifferentiated, differ in their own respective characteristics and so co-arise together within a single body without conflict, so too do the store-consciousness and the active consciousnesses co-arise together within a single body without conflict.
Third, the torrent and the rest; first, the similes; first, the simile of waves. Just as a single raging torrent has many waves moving at once without conflict.
Second, the simile of reflections. Just as a single clear mirror surface has many reflections appearing at once without conflict.
Second, applying the simile. So too does a single store-consciousness have many active consciousnesses co-arising at once without conflict.
Second, similes for simultaneous co-arising; first, the similes; first, the simile of the eye-consciousness and the rest; first, the eye-consciousness. Just as a single eye-consciousness, at one time, takes in only a single uniform colour with respect to one object, and at another time, takes in many varied colours at once.
Second, the ear-consciousness and the rest. As with the eye-consciousness regarding colours, so too with the ear-consciousness regarding sounds, the nose-consciousness regarding scents, and the tongue-consciousness regarding flavours.
Second, the simile of the body-consciousness and the rest; first, the body-consciousness. Just as the body-consciousness, at one time, takes in only a single uniform tactile sensation, and at another time, takes in many varied tactile sensations at once.
Second, the discerning mental consciousness. So too does the discerning mental consciousness, at one time, take in a single object, or take in many varied objects at once.
Second, applying the simile. Know that the underlying principle here is likewise without conflict.

items.title: Section: Four Afflictions Manas Never Sheds — Self-View, Self-Pride, Self-Love, and Ignorance

items.zh: 又前說末那恒與阿賴耶識俱轉，乃至未斷，當知常與俱生任運四種煩惱一時相應。謂薩迦耶見、我慢、我愛，及與無明。此四煩惱，若在定地，若不定地，當知恒行，不與善等相違，是有覆無記性。
items.en:
Second, manas's own aspect of co-arising with the store-consciousness; first, listing its correspondence. As already said, manas constantly co-arises with the store-consciousness; until self-grasping is severed, know that it constantly, spontaneously corresponds with four afflictions at once: the view of a perishable self, self-pride, self-love, and ignorance.
Second, further examining these characteristics. These four afflictions operate constantly whether in a state of concentration or not, and, being of a concealing yet neutral nature, do not conflict with wholesome and other karma.

items.title: Section: The Fifth and Final Aspect Opens — Why the Store-Consciousness Is the Root of All Defilement

items.zh: 如是阿賴耶識，與轉識俱轉故，與諸受俱轉故，與善等俱轉故，應知建立阿賴耶識俱轉轉相。云何建立阿賴耶識雜染還滅相？謂略說阿賴耶識是一切雜染根本。所以者何？由此識是有情世間生起根本，能生諸根、根所依處及轉識等故。亦是器世間生起根本，由能生起器世間故。亦是有情互起根本，一切有情相望互為增上緣故。所以者何？無有有情與餘有情互相見等時，不生苦樂等更相受用。由此道理，當知有情界互為增上緣。
items.en:
Second, concluding the essential meaning. Through co-arising with the active consciousnesses, with their feelings, and with their moral qualities, one should understand the establishment of the store-consciousness's own co-arising.
Fifth, the turning of defilement and its reversal; first, posing the question. How is the store-consciousness's own turning of defilement and its reversal established?
Second, explaining; first, clarifying establishment; first, distinguishing characteristics individually; first, the root of defilement; first, briefly distinguishing; first, distinguishing differences; first, distinguishing by the fruit produced; first, stating. In brief, the store-consciousness is the root of all defilement.
Second, posing the question. Why is this?
Third, explaining; first, the world of sentient beings. Because this consciousness is the root from which the world of sentient beings arises, giving rise to the sense faculties, their physical basis, and the active consciousnesses.
Second, the physical environment. It is likewise the root from which the physical environment arises, since it gives rise to that environment.
Third, the mutual influence of beings; first, stating this mutual conditioning. It is also the root of beings' mutual arising, since all beings serve as a supportive condition for one another.
Second, explaining why. Why is this? There is no case of one being encountering another without some feeling of pleasure or displeasure arising between them. By this reasoning, know that beings serve as a mutual supportive condition for one another.

items.title: Section: Wholesome Roots That Run Against the Current — Why Seeds Conforming to Liberation Are Never the Cause of Suffering's Own Accumulation

items.zh: 又即此阿賴耶識能持一切法種子故，於現在世是苦諦體，亦是未來苦諦生因，又是現在集諦生因。如是能生有情世間故，能生器世間故，是苦諦體故，能生未來苦諦故，能生現在集諦故，當知阿賴耶識是一切雜染根本。復次，阿賴耶識所攝持順解脫分及順決擇分等善法種子，此非集諦因。由順解脫分等善根與流轉相違故。
items.en:
Second, distinguishing by holding seeds. Also, this same store-consciousness, holding the seeds of every phenomenon, in the present constitutes the very substance of the truth of suffering; it is also the generative cause of the future truth of suffering, and the generative cause of the present truth of accumulation.
Second, concluding the essential meaning. Through giving rise to the world of sentient beings, the physical environment, constituting the substance of suffering, and generating the future truth of suffering and the present truth of accumulation, know that the store-consciousness is the root of all defilement.
Second, distinguishing individually; first, stating this nature. Furthermore, the wholesome seeds held by the store-consciousness that conform to liberation and conform to the determination of the path are not the cause of the truth of accumulation.
Second, explaining this exception. Because such wholesome roots conforming to liberation run counter to the current of saṃsāra's own turning.

items.title: Section: A Cluster of Sacred Fruit — Why the Store-Consciousness's Own Seeds Are Truly Without Limit

items.zh: 善根，因此生故，轉更明盛。由此因緣，彼所攝受自類種子轉有功能、轉有勢力，增長種子，速得成立。復由此種子故，彼諸善法轉明盛生。又復能感當來轉增、轉勝可愛可樂諸異熟果。復次，依此一切種子阿賴耶識故，薄伽梵說：有眼界、色界、眼識界，乃至有意界、法界、意識界。由於阿賴耶識中有種種界故。又如經說惡叉聚喻。由於阿賴耶識中有多界故。
items.en:
Second, regarding the fruit of wholesome karma. Also because of these seeds, those wholesome dharmas grow ever more radiant and vigorous, and are also able to bring about future ripened results ever more increased and excellent, desirable and delightful.
Third, citing scriptural proof; first, having various elements. Furthermore, relying on this store-consciousness that holds every seed, the Blessed One said: there is the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element, and so on through the mind-element, the phenomena-element, and the mental-consciousness-element — because the store-consciousness has such various elements, in the sense of causes, that is, seeds.
Second, having many elements. And as a sūtra speaks of the akṣa-cluster simile — because the store-consciousness has many elements, again in the sense of seeds.

items.title: Section: Only Genuine Wholesome Practice Can Transform the Root of Defilement Itself

items.zh: 復次，此雜染根本阿賴耶識，修善法故，方得轉滅。
items.en:
Second, the causes and conditions of transformation and extinguishing; first, stating in brief. Furthermore, this store-consciousness, the root of defilement, is transformed and extinguished only through cultivating wholesome dharma.
Commentary: as for cultivating wholesome dharma — this wholesome dharma refers to the very wholesome roots already explained as conforming to liberation and conforming to the path's own determination.

items.title: Section: Three Kinds of Attention — From the Fire-Drill's First Spark to Breaking Free of Both Bondages

items.zh: 此修善法，若諸異生，以緣轉識為境作意，方便住心，能入最初聖諦現觀。非未見諦者，於諸諦中未得法眼，便能通達一切種子阿賴耶識。此未見諦者修如是行已，或入聲聞正性離生，或入菩薩正性離生，達一切法真法界已，亦能通達阿賴耶識。當於爾時，能總觀察自內所有一切雜染，亦能了知自身外為相縛所縛，內為麁重縛所縛。
items.en:
Second, distinguishing individually; first, entering attention. In this cultivation of wholesome dharma, an ordinary being takes the active consciousnesses as the object of attention, settling the mind through skilful means, and is thereby able to enter the very first direct realisation of the noble truths.
Second, penetrating attention; first, stating the stage. One who has not yet seen the truths, not yet attained the dharma-eye regarding them, cannot penetrate the store-consciousness holding every seed.
One who has not yet seen the truths, having practised in this way, enters either the śrāvaka's own true nature free of rebirth or the bodhisattva's own true nature free of rebirth, and, having penetrated the true dharma-realm of all phenomena, is then also able to penetrate the store-consciousness.
Second, distinguishing the characteristics. At that very time, one is able to comprehensively observe every defilement within oneself, and also to recognise that one is outwardly bound by the bondage of appearances, and inwardly bound by the bondage of coarse afflictive residue.

blocks.text: How the store-consciousness lies at the root of both saṃsāra and its reversal.

The torrent and the mirror are the store-consciousness; the waves and reflections are the active consciousnesses. (Untranslated, 0580c24: the store-consciousness operates at the same time as wholesome, unwholesome, and neutral mental factors, yet should not be said to be associated with them.)
The view of self, self-pride, self-love, and ignorance. Master Cháng Bǎi: manas is subtle yet obstructs the path, hence "concealing".
It is the root of the world of beings, of the environment, and of their mutual arising. Master Cháng Bǎi: past ties differ, so present feelings differ; an arhat remains in supreme equanimity.

Master Cháng Bǎi: its seeds yield the present body and world, and it keeps strengthening the seeds of craving and views. Yet some wholesome roots "run counter to saṃsāra": the first belongs to the stage of provisions, the second to the stage of preparation.
Master Cháng Bǎi: 界 here means cause, seed; the akṣa fruit grows three on one stem, like delusion, karma, and suffering.
Only cultivating wholesome dharma transforms it. Master Cháng Bǎi: the power comes from the pure seeds planted in it.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the object is the images appearing to one's own sixth consciousness, reflecting on suchness; these are the four stages of preparation. The dharma-eye is wisdom seeing reality as it is; the coarse residue is the seeds of affliction, which leave practice incapable.
The waves-and-torrent image became central to East Asian Buddhism. The waves are not separate from the water, yet they are not the water's whole depth.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi map the torrent and mirror similes?
options: torrent and mirror: store-consciousness; waves and reflections: active consciousnesses
quiz.why: Torrent and mirror are the store-consciousness; waves and reflections the active consciousnesses.

quiz.q: With which four afflictions does manas constantly correspond?
options: view of a perishable self, self-pride, self-love, ignorance
quiz.why: The view of self, self-pride, self-love, ignorance. Master Cháng Bǎi: manas is subtle yet obstructs the path, hence "concealing."

quiz.q: Of what is it the root?
options: the world of beings, the environment, and beings' mutual arising
quiz.why: Of the world of beings, the environment, and mutual arising.

quiz.q: Beings condition each other; why do feelings differ on meeting?
options: past ties differ; an arhat stays in equanimity, undefiled
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: past ties differ, so present feelings differ; an arhat remains in supreme equanimity.

quiz.q: Why is it both the substance of suffering and a cause of accumulation now?
options: its seeds yield present results, so suffering; it strengthens seeds of craving and views, so accumulation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: its seeds yield the present body and environment; it keeps strengthening seeds of craving and views.

quiz.q: Why aren't seeds conforming to liberation a cause of accumulation?
options: they run counter to saṃsāra's turning
quiz.why: They run counter to saṃsāra. Master Cháng Bǎi: the first belongs to the provisions stage, the second to the stage of preparatory effort.

quiz.q: "Various elements" and the akṣa-cluster: how does Master Cháng Bǎi explain?
options: 界 means cause, seed; the akṣa fruit grows in threes, like delusion, karma, and suffering
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 界 means cause, seed; the akṣa fruit grows three on one stem, like delusion, karma, and suffering. "Element" hides the sense of seed.
Only through cultivating wholesome dharma. Master Cháng Bǎi: the power of cause is the pure seeds habituated in it.

quiz.q: "Taking the active consciousnesses as object." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain?
options: the images of one's own sixth consciousness, reflecting on suchness
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the object is the images appearing to one's own sixth consciousness, reflecting on suchness; these are the four preparatory stages.

options: one who hasn't seen the truths, lacking the dharma-eye
quiz.why: One who hasn't seen the truths. Master Cháng Bǎi: the dharma-eye is wisdom seeing reality as it is.

quiz.q: What is "coarse residue" per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: seeds of affliction, leaving ordinary beings incapable in practice
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: coarse residue is the seeds of affliction, which leave practice incapable.
